questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and Correcting Statements

subQuestions.questionText:
The marketing process involves …
A. determining the product the consumer wants.
B. determining the product of interest to the supplier.
C. management of sales volume.
D. planning based on current products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - determining the product the consumer wants (2 marks)
The marketing concept starts with the needs and wants of the consumer, then produces to satisfy them.

options.A: determining the product the consumer wants.
options.B: determining the product of interest to the supplier.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following statements is NOT CORRECT about factors that hamper the marketing of agricultural products:
A. Poor infrastructure
B. Perishability of the product
C. High value in relation to volume
D. Wide distribution of the product
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - High value in relation to volume (2 marks)
It is a LOW value in relation to volume (bulkiness) that hampers marketing, not a high value.

options.C: High value in relation to volume

subQuestions.questionText:
A channel where products are advertised to a global consumer with upfront payment, is … marketing.
A. contract
B. farm gate
C. stock sale
D. internet
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - internet (2 marks)
Internet marketing reaches a global consumer base and usually requires payment before the goods are dispatched.

subQuestions.questionText:
The downward sloping curve to the right in a market implies that:
(i) As the price of a product rises, the quantity demanded drops.
(ii) When the price of a product rises, the supply remains constant.
(iii) There is an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded.
(iv) The quantity demanded is high as the price of a product is low.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
B. (i), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (ii) and (iii)
D. (i), (ii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
A downward-sloping demand curve shows an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded. Statement (ii) refers to supply and is not implied by the demand curve.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following is NOT a method to improve productivity of land:
A. Intercropping
B. Improving soil fertility
C. Monocropping
D. Restoring land potential
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Monocropping (2 marks)
Growing the same crop repeatedly on the same land (monocropping) depletes nutrients and lowers productivity.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following is NOT a source of capital:
A. Risk factor
B. Trust company
C. Business partner
D. Land Bank
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Risk factor (2 marks)
Trust companies, business partners and the Land Bank all provide capital. A risk factor is not a source of capital.

subQuestions.questionText:
A farmer may apply the measures below to increase labour productivity on the farm:
(i) Have the correct type and number of workers
(ii) Set clear unattainable goals for workers
(iii) Give workers the opportunity to be involved in decision-making
(iv) Ensure the welfare of workers
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (i), (iii) and (iv)
C. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iii)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Setting 'unattainable' goals (ii) demotivates workers and lowers productivity, so it is excluded.

subQuestions.questionText:
The external force which can affect a farming business:
A. Quality and cost of a product
B. Available equipment and machinery
C. Amount of debt a farmer has at a bank
D. Policies about the labour force
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Policies about the labour force (2 marks)
Government labour policies are an external (legal/political) force beyond the farmer's control. The other options are internal factors.

options.A: Quality and cost of a product
options.C: Amount of debt a farmer has at a bank

subQuestions.questionText:
If a homozygous dominant tall plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant (tt), the genotypic and phenotypic percentages of tall plants in the F1-generation will be …
A. 50%.
B. 100%.
C. 75%.
D. 25%.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - 100% (2 marks)
TT × tt gives all Tt offspring: 100% are heterozygous (genotype) and 100% are tall (phenotype).

subQuestions.questionText:
The illustration in the question paper demonstrates an example of … in chromosomal mutation (it shows a tetraploid cell and a hexaploid cell, i.e. cells with multiple whole sets of chromosomes).
A. haploidy
B. pentaploidy
C. polyploidy
D. diploidy
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - polyploidy (2 marks)
Polyploidy is the condition of having more than two complete sets of chromosomes (e.g. tetraploid = 4 sets, hexaploid = 6 sets).

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Marketing strategy that targets the whole market with a single offer.
COLUMN B options: A. storage  B. XX and XY  C. both the farmer and the farm worker contribute  D. depreciation  E. multisegmented marketing  F. X-linked and Y-linked characteristics  G. appreciation  H. value adding  I. only the farmer contributes  J. mass marketing
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: J - mass marketing (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Keeping goods until they are needed for future use and to guarantee food security.
COLUMN B options: A. storage  B. XX and XY  C. both the farmer and the farm worker contribute  D. depreciation  E. multisegmented marketing  F. X-linked and Y-linked characteristics  G. appreciation  H. value adding  I. only the farmer contributes  J. mass marketing
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A - storage (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Unemployment Insurance Fund.
COLUMN B options: A. storage  B. XX and XY  C. both the farmer and the farm worker contribute  D. depreciation  E. multisegmented marketing  F. X-linked and Y-linked characteristics  G. appreciation  H. value adding  I. only the farmer contributes  J. mass marketing
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - both the farmer and the farm worker contribute (2 marks)
Both employer and employee pay a monthly contribution to the UIF.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The value of assets increases over time.
COLUMN B options: A. storage  B. XX and XY  C. both the farmer and the farm worker contribute  D. depreciation  E. multisegmented marketing  F. X-linked and Y-linked characteristics  G. appreciation  H. value adding  I. only the farmer contributes  J. mass marketing
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: G - appreciation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Sex chromosomes.
COLUMN B options: A. storage  B. XX and XY  C. both the farmer and the farm worker contribute  D. depreciation  E. multisegmented marketing  F. X-linked and Y-linked characteristics  G. appreciation  H. value adding  I. only the farmer contributes  J. mass marketing
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - XX and XY (2 marks)
The sex chromosomes are XX (female) and XY (male).

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A long-term plan that enables the manager to minimise the risk of losing production due to drought.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Strategic risk management (strategic planning) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A measure of output per unit of input.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Productivity (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A situation where one parent has more homozygous dominant alleles for certain traits which are passed on to offspring than the other parent.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Prepotency (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The use of statistics for analysing biological data.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Biometrics (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
Herbicide-resistant hybrid plants that are the products of a cross between wild plants and genetically modified crops.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Super weeds (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Market mix is the result of the interaction between the supply and demand of goods and services.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Price determination (price) (1 mark)
The interaction of supply and demand determines the price. The marketing mix is the combination of product, price, place and promotion.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Cost is the money paid over and above the amount borrowed.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Interest (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
A dominant allele is not expressed in the phenotype of a heterozygous organism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Recessive (allele) (1 mark)
It is the recessive allele that is masked (not expressed) in a heterozygote; the dominant allele is expressed.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
The mating of a pure-bred bull with inferior cows, generation after generation, refers to inbreeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Upgrading (grading up) (1 mark)
Using a pure-bred bull on inferior cows over successive generations to raise the quality of the herd is upgrading.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Breeding value is a form of technology that involves highly advanced scientific techniques of inserting genes to obtain desirable characteristics.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Genetic modification (also: GM / genetic engineering / genetic manipulation) (1 mark)

questions.title: Section B, Question 2: Agricultural Management and Marketing

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two illustrations in the question paper represent supply and demand in a market. ILLUSTRATION A has price on one axis and 'PRODUCT AVAILABILITY' on the other; ILLUSTRATION B has price on one axis and 'PRODUCT PURCHASED' on the other.
Identify the illustration that represents demand.
subQuestions.memoText: Illustration B (product purchased vs price = demand). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the illustration (A or B) that represents supply.
subQuestions.memoText: Illustration A (product availability vs price = supply). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the law applicable to ILLUSTRATION B (product purchased in relation to price).
subQuestions.memoText: The law of demand: the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded; the lower the price, the higher the quantity demanded. Price is inversely proportional to demand. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors that influence the illustration in A (supply), other than price.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Production / labour / input costs
• Technology
• Subsidies / taxation
• Possibility of increasing supply
• Demand for the product
• Environmental conditions / nature
• Availability of the product
• Competitive products
• Profit margin of the product
• Stability (storability) of the product
• Knowledge / research
• Political instability
• Number of suppliers
• Legislation
• Seasonality of the product

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two graphs in the question paper show the response of quantity demanded to a change in price. GRAPH A: a large change in price (P1 to P2) causes a large change in quantity demanded (Q1 to Q2). GRAPH B: a large change in price causes only a small change in quantity demanded.
Indicate the type of elasticity illustrated in Graph A.
subQuestions.memoText: Price elastic (elastic demand). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the type of elasticity illustrated in Graph B.
subQuestions.memoText: Price inelastic (inelastic demand). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.2.1(a) (Graph A).
subQuestions.memoText: The change in price results in a huge (proportionally larger) change in quantity demanded. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that could have led to the situation illustrated in GRAPH A (elastic demand).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Nature of the product (luxury vs necessity)
• Availability of substitute products
• Consumer's budget / income
• Time period considered

subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper shows a system used to market agricultural products, captioned 'CONNECTS FARMERS TO CUSTOMERS' (farmers selling directly to buyers without government control).
Identify the marketing system represented in the picture.
subQuestions.memoText: Free marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From the picture above, deduce TWO advantages of the marketing system identified in QUESTION 2.3.1 (free marketing) for the buyer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Buyers get good-quality products
• Elimination of agents leads to lower prices
• Buyers can bargain
• Buyers can buy where they want
• Convenient to buyers

subQuestions.questionText: Give the economic term referring to the phenomenon where producers negotiate prices artificially rather than competing freely.
subQuestions.memoText: Price fixing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO principles of agricultural co-operatives.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Voluntary and open membership
• Democratic member control
• Equal economic participation by members
• Autonomy and independence
• Provision of education, training and information to members
• Co-operation among co-operatives
• Concern for the community
• Marketing is based on a pool system
• Members have a single vote
• Members are paid dividends / limited interest on their share capital
• Only members may deliver products

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the case study: A farmer owning one hectare of land saw an opportunity to start a small business of producing eggs to sell to the community. Despite two break-ins and a scarcity of water, the farmer continued with the business. Determination, resilience and passion kept the farmer going.
The farmer in the case study is an entrepreneur. Justify this statement by giving a reason from the case study.
subQuestions.memoText: The farmer saw an opportunity to start a business and took a risk (continued despite break-ins and water scarcity). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO entrepreneurial success factors of the farmer in the case study above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): determination; resilience; passion; being an opportunist. (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 2.4.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example from the case study of a strength of the enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): the good qualities of the entrepreneur (determination, resilience, passion); owning one hectare of land.

subQuestions.label: 2.4.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example from the case study of a threat to the enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): break-ins (theft); scarcity of water.

subQuestions.label: 2.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two diagrams in the question paper represent an agricultural marketing chain. DIAGRAM A links: Marketing → Sales → Customer service (customer-facing, pull). DIAGRAM B links: Purchasing of inputs → Production → Distribution (producer-facing, push).
Indicate the type of agricultural marketing chain represented by DIAGRAM A.
subQuestions.memoText: Demand chain (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the type of agricultural marketing chain represented by DIAGRAM B (Purchasing of inputs → Production → Distribution).
subQuestions.memoText: Supply chain (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the agricultural marketing chain (DIAGRAM A or DIAGRAM B) described by the statement:
(a) Efficiency focused, short-term orientated, planning and control.
subQuestions.memoText: DIAGRAM B (supply chain) (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the agricultural marketing chain (DIAGRAM A or DIAGRAM B) described by the statement:
(b) Focus on effectiveness, long-term orientated, demand, management and supply.
subQuestions.memoText: DIAGRAM A (demand chain) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO ways that farmers can use to streamline and improve the agribusiness chain.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Use of cold storage and refrigerated transport
• Grading and standardisation of products
• Marketing collectively by combining loads with other farmers
• Processing of products closer to the farm
• Improving road infrastructure
• Improving access to market information
• Making storage facilities available
• Providing access to finance
• Improving cell-phone and internet connectivity

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO roles of legislation in the effective marketing of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Promotes efficient marketing of agricultural products
• Ensures minimum marketing interventions
• Increases market access to all participants
• Enhances the viability of the agricultural sector
• Regulates / quality-controls import and export products
• Prevents unfair marketing practices / consumer exploitation
• Ensures product information is given in simple language
• Ensures products comply with set standards / product safety
• Sets and maintains national standards at processing sites
• Regulates market agents and improves their functioning
• Authorises the establishment of marketing regulations

subQuestions.questionText:
Before starting a farming enterprise, a document describing the business and its goals and objectives should be developed.
Identify the document in the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Business plan (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for developing the document identified in QUESTION 2.7.1 (a business plan).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Test the feasibility and economic viability of the business idea
• Determine the financial needs
• Reposition the business to deal with market changes
• Gain knowledge about marketing opportunities and competitors
• Foresee problems, which reduces risk
• Guide daily operations / roles and responsibilities
• Secure funding
• Ensure effective business management
• Map out objectives and goals
• Provide guidelines for decision making
• Provide time frames for completion of projects
• Provide information about the business

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO problems that a farmer may encounter when drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Insufficient technical details
• Unrealistic assumptions and projections / overambitious
• Leaving gaps / being vague / errors / too generic / too much unnecessary information
• Hiding weaknesses and risks
• Incomplete financials / forgetting the cash flow
• Insufficient research
• Using an incorrect format
• Not including information about suppliers
• Not highlighting potential competition

subQuestions.questionText:
All the production factors are important and should be well managed in order to maximise production.
Name a production factor that is durable and found in a specific environment.
subQuestions.memoText: Land (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO economic functions of the production factor named in QUESTION 3.1.1 (land).
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): provides food; provides space; provides raw materials; provides minerals; serves as collateral.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below illustrates the quantity of fertiliser applied and maize production.
Fertiliser (kg) | Maize production (kg)
1  | 8
5  | 20
10 | 35
15 | 38
20 | 39
25 | 39
Identify the economic characteristic of land illustrated in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: The law of diminishing returns (1 mark)
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Compare the maize production response to increased fertiliser application from 1 kg to 10 kg.
subQuestions.memoText: With the increase in fertiliser from 1 kg to 10 kg, maize production increases at an increasing rate (large gains: 8 → 20 → 35 kg). (1 mark)
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Compare the maize production response to increased fertiliser application from 15 kg to 20 kg.
subQuestions.memoText: With the increase in fertiliser from 15 kg to 20 kg, maize production increases at a decreasing rate (small gain: 38 → 39 kg). (1 mark)
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows duties performed by two different workers on the farm.
WORKER 1: Building a dam; Erecting a fence; Painting farm buildings.
WORKER 2: Shearing sheep; Picking avocadoes; Harvesting grapes.
Identify the type of temporary worker represented by WORKER 1.
subQuestions.memoText: Casual worker (once-off tasks). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of temporary worker represented by WORKER 2 (shearing sheep, picking avocadoes, harvesting grapes).
subQuestions.memoText: Seasonal worker (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.3.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText: Worker 2 performs repetitive tasks that occur at a specific time of the year (harvest / shearing season). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways to increase labour productivity in agriculture.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Improve the economic conditions of workers
• Improve education / training
• Improve working conditions
• Improve living conditions
• Address HIV/AIDS
• Manage / supervise labour effectively
• Efficient mechanisation
• Proper planning
• Involve workers in decision making
• Motivation

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
An extract from a contract of employment is shown: 1. Job title: Driver. 2. Duration of contract: 1 February 2021 to retirement. 3. Mode of payment: Payment into bank account (monthly). 4. Remuneration: Minimum wage for the specific area. 5. Terms of employment: 5.1 Working hours 08:00–17:00; 5.2 Leave: as prescribed by legislation. 6. Protective clothing: None. (Signature blocks for employee and employer.)
Select an item from the contract that relates to the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 75 of 1997).
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): duration of contract (1 Feb 2021 – retirement); remuneration / amount; terms of employment / leave / working hours; mode of payment.

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Select an item from the contract of employment above that relates to the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993).
subQuestions.memoText: Protective clothing (item 6: 'None'). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which migration of labour from farms to other industries will decrease production in a farming enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• It leads to labour shortages
• It leads to a shortage of skills / expertise / experience

subQuestions.questionText:
A schematic representation in the question paper shows types of capital with examples, labelled A, B and C (A: land, buildings, dams; B: tractors, implements, vehicles, livestock; C: seed, fuel, feed, fertiliser, wages).
Identify the types of capital represented by A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Fixed capital (1 mark)
B - Movable capital (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of a capital item represented by C (working / production capital) in the schematic representation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): seed / fuel / feed / wages / fertiliser / chemicals / transport costs.

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Suggest the type of credit that can be sourced from a financial institution to acquire the type of capital represented by A (fixed capital).
subQuestions.memoText: Long-term credit (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Suggest the type of credit that can be sourced from a financial institution to acquire the type of capital represented by C (working / production capital).
subQuestions.memoText: Short-term credit (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE method of creating capital.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): production (reinvesting profit); savings; credit / loans; grants / sponsors / donations; inheritance / trust funds; partnerships.

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A graph in the question paper shows total income and total expenditure for three farming enterprises (A, B and C) for the 2023/24 financial year (values roughly: A income R30 000 / expenses R50 000; B income R60 000 / expenses R40 000; C income R45 000 / expenses R20 000).
Identify the enterprise with the highest income.
subQuestions.memoText: Enterprise B (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the enterprise in the graph above with the lowest expenses.
subQuestions.memoText: Enterprise C (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the financial record that shows the information in the data above (income and expenditure per enterprise, giving profit or loss).
subQuestions.memoText: Income statement (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the profit or loss for enterprise A. Show ALL the calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Profit/Loss = Total income − Total expenses
= R30 000 − R50 000
= −R20 000 (a loss of R20 000) (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
State the problem associated with capital that is applicable to the statement:
The farmer does not have enough capital to buy equipment to run the farming enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText: Scarcity / shortage of capital (capital is expensive / costly). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State the problem associated with capital that is applicable to the statement:
Too much capital is invested in the enterprise in relation to available land and labour.
subQuestions.memoText: Overcapitalisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario: The farmer took the opportunity of having an orchard to start a business making jam and dried and canned fruit. The business was growing until the machinery broke down, resulting in a drop in sales. The farmer then introduced a piggery, poultry, sheep farming and sold manure to other farmers and community members.
Identify TWO sources of risk in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): production risk; technical risk; financial / market and price risk.

subQuestions.questionText: Justify EACH source of risk identified in QUESTION 3.8.1 based on the scenario.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Production risk – the environment / breakdowns pose a risk to production
• Technical risk – the machinery broke down
• Financial / market and price risk – loss of sales

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the risk management strategy used by the farmer to deal with the risks identified in QUESTION 3.8.1 (introducing a piggery, poultry, sheep and manure sales).
subQuestions.memoText: Diversification (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE applicable management principle that would assist the farmer to manage the risks.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): planning; organisation / co-ordination; decision making; implementation; control.

questions.title: Section B, Question 4: Basic Agricultural Genetics

subQuestions.questionText:
In pea plants, spherical seeds (S) are dominant over dented seeds (s). Two heterozygous plants (Ss) were crossed. The Punnett square gives offspring SS, Ss, Ss, ss.
Indicate the fraction of the offspring that will have dented seeds.
subQuestions.memoText: 1/4 (only the ss offspring has dented seeds). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of heterozygous spherical seeds from the Ss × Ss cross (offspring SS, Ss, Ss, ss).
subQuestions.memoText:
= 2/4 × 100
= 50% (the two Ss offspring). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the phenotypic ratio of the F1-generation (from the Ss × Ss cross).
subQuestions.memoText: 3 spherical : 1 dented (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the number of offspring that will look similar to the parents (heterozygous spherical) from the Ss × Ss cross.
subQuestions.memoText: Phenotypically 3 (all spherical-seeded); genotypically 2 (the two Ss). (Any 1) (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two illustrations show the crossing of different flowers. ILLUSTRATION A: RR (red) × WW (white) → offspring RW, which is pink. ILLUSTRATION B: a cross involving alleles R and W → offspring RW, which shows both red and white patches.
Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by ILLUSTRATION B.
subQuestions.memoText: Co-dominance (both alleles fully expressed — red and white patches). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by ILLUSTRATION A (RR red × WW white → pink RW offspring).
subQuestions.memoText: Incomplete dominance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answer to QUESTION 4.2.1(b) (incomplete dominance in ILLUSTRATION A).
subQuestions.memoText: The offspring has an intermediate characteristic (pink), a blend between the red and white parents. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the genotype of the offspring in ILLUSTRATION B.
subQuestions.memoText: RW (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Quantitative characteristics are controlled by many pairs of genes and show continuous variation; qualitative characteristics are controlled by one pair of genes and fall into clear-cut categories.
Indicate whether height is a qualitative or quantitative characteristic.
subQuestions.memoText: Quantitative characteristic (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether horn conformation is a qualitative or quantitative characteristic.
subQuestions.memoText: Qualitative characteristic (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether milk production is a qualitative or quantitative characteristic.
subQuestions.memoText: Quantitative characteristic (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper shows an ewe with her triplets, each lamb a different colour.
Identify the phenomenon visible with regard to the colour of each of the triplets.
subQuestions.memoText: Variation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State whether the phenomenon in the picture above (different lamb colours) is environmental or genetic.
subQuestions.memoText: Genetic (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE cause that could have led to the phenomenon (variation) in the triplets above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): meiosis / crossing over / random arrangement of chromosomes; random fertilisation; mutation.

subQuestions.questionText: State the importance of the phenomenon identified in QUESTION 4.4.1 (variation), in a breeding programme.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): it forms the foundation of selection and breeding; it allows breeds / cultivars to be improved over time; it increases biodiversity.

subQuestions.questionText:
A farmer crossed two cultivars, CULTIVAR A (PPLL) and CULTIVAR B (ppll), to improve the characteristics of CULTIVAR B. P = purple seed, p = yellow seed, L = long leaf, l = short leaf.
Identify ONE characteristic that the farmer needs to improve.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): leaf length (short → long); seed colour (yellow → purple).

subQuestions.questionText: Use a Punnett square to show the F1-generation of the cross between CULTIVAR A (PPLL) and CULTIVAR B (ppll).
subQuestions.memoText:
Gametes of CULTIVAR A: PL, PL. Gametes of CULTIVAR B: pl, pl.
Punnett square offspring: PpLl, PpLl, PpLl, PpLl.
Marking rubric (1 mark each): correct gametes of the one parent; correct gametes of the other parent; correct genotype of the offspring (PpLl); completed Punnett square populated with gametes and offspring.
The entire F1-generation is PpLl.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the law that applies during gamete formation in QUESTION 4.5.2 before crossing is done.
subQuestions.memoText: The law of independent assortment (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.6.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A schematic representation shows different breeding systems in cattle, with animals numbered 1–14.
Identify the breeding system illustrated if animal 1 is a Hereford and mates with animal 2 that is a Shorthorn.
subQuestions.memoText: Crossbreeding (crossing two different breeds). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.6.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the breeding system illustrated if animal 3 mates with animal 4 and both are Holstein pure breeds that are not related.
subQuestions.memoText: Outcrossing (mating unrelated animals of the same breed). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage that animals 12, 13 and 14 (the crossbred offspring) will have over their parents.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Crossbreds exhibit heterosis / hybrid vigour
• More resistant to diseases
• More vitality / fertility
• Perform better than their parents
• More economic production (higher mass gain relative to feed intake)
• Better adaptability to environmental conditions

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE selection method that could be used in the animal breeding systems identified in QUESTION 4.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): mass selection; family selection; pedigree selection; progeny selection.

subQuestions.questionText:
A flow chart in the question paper illustrates a technique used in plant breeding, in which genes are transferred into a plant using a soil bacterium as a vector.
Identify the plant breeding technique illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: The use of bacterial carriers (Agrobacterium tumefaciens). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO potential environmental benefits of GM crops.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Reduce the need for chemical spraying / herbicides / pollution
• Tolerant to extreme conditions (cold / drought / salinity)
• Beneficial insects are not harmed
• Allows for no-till farming

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below represents the yield of genetically modified (GM) maize and non-GM maize in different provinces.
Province | Non-GM maize yield (kg/ha) | GM maize yield (kg/ha)
A | 3 500 | 4 500
B | 5 500 | 8 000
C | 8 000 | 9 500
D | 8 500 | 10 000
E | 4 500 | 6 000
Draw a line graph showing the yields of GM maize and non-GM maize in the different provinces on the same set of axes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Combined line graph. Marking rubric (1 mark each):
• Correct heading with both variables
• X-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Province)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Yield)
• Correct units (kg/ha)
• Combined line graph (two lines: GM maize and non-GM maize)
• Accuracy (80%+ correctly plotted); the GM line lies above the non-GM line for every province
